title: Samsung Securities says attachments with personal data of 8,241 customers leaked from its VOC service
date_note: Samsung Securities' customer notice, as reported by Dailysecu, says an unauthorized outsider accessed the VOC intake service on the afternoon of 21 November 2026.
summary: Samsung Securities said in a customer notice, reported by Dailysecu, that an unauthorized outsider accessed its website's VOC (customer complaint) intake service by abnormal means on the afternoon of 21 November, and attachments containing personal data of 8,241 customers leaked. According to Dailysecu, 13 items leaked, including name, account number and driver's licence number. The company says it blocked the IP address, suspended the service and is investigating the cause.
plain: Samsung Securities says someone got into its customer complaint service and took uploaded files holding personal data of 8,241 customers.
exec: A securities broker's complaint-intake web service leaked customer attachments with personal data of 8,241 customers.
action: Samsung Securities advises customers to check the leaked items in the website's personal (credit) information leak lookup menu and to beware of voice-phishing calls and spam emails meant to deliver malware.
geo_basis: country only; the page read gives no city, pinned at Seoul as the country's capital

evidence.quote: Information on 8,241 clients had been leaked after the firm found unauthorized access to its customer response system, Samsung Securities confirmed.

validation.note: Dailysecu (quoting the customer notice) and The Korea Herald (relaying Yonhap) each state that data of 8,241 Samsung Securities customers leaked after unauthorized access; the notice itself was not found online.

review.note: Compared title, date, 8,241 customers, 13 items, IP block, service suspension and customer advice against the Dailysecu article; single_source status fits
